goal: A static Rust binary that reads what an agent produced and refuses the growth that should not be there, deleted or weakened tests, skips, stubs, swallowed errors, secrets, guardrail edits, dependency-direction violations, in milliseconds, with zero tokens, every finding as SARIF 2.1.0. `weed check` judges a diff and may block; `weed scan` judges the tree and never blocks; `weed guard` is the law in git through hooks; `weed bite` proves a test fails without its change. ## The goal
The rules that read the change to a test suite and name each way it can become weaker without anyone deleting a test: assertions dropped, a tolerance widened, expected values regenerated, an error assertion loosened, a test uncollected by rename, and a mock placed over the very unit under change. T2 blocks by default; the rest warn, for the human at the pull request. Each lands as a failing fixture first in TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Rust and Go, with a silent neighbour.

- You are at the repository root of an isolated git worktree. Work here directly.
- Leave your changes in the working tree; do not create branches, commit, or push.
- The loop file (docs/tend2/rules-tests.tend2.html) is your full context — read it, including its narrative. It is READ-ONLY for you.

- (code) T2 follows an assertion that left a changed test file into the rest of the diff, by the case it sat in or the same line under a rename, counts only what did not arrive anywhere, and its message says behaviour is held by nobody only when none of the lost assertions arrived, naming the files they moved into otherwise, in ts, py, rs and go · evidence expected at: tests/rule_t2.rs

    tend2 verify docs/tend2/rules-tests.tend2.html --repo-root . --force --expect-payload 2a80e1353044 --runner 'bash scripts/check/run.sh {evidence}'
